**What broke (Thursday, Nov 12):** The ingest v2.14.0 deploy at 08:47 UTC raised the default `max_batch_bytes` from 1 MB to 10 MB (PR ingest#412), while ingest-worker pods run with a 512 Mi memory limit — so the workers OOM-looped and the Kafka consumer lag climbed to over 500k messages [3][9]. It was a SEV2; dashboards ran stale from 08:47 to 12:27 UTC (3h40, peaking ~3h40 behind) [1][3][7]. It was not the Kafka brokers (disk was fine at 62%) [3].

**Data loss:** No. Events kept arriving in Kafka and were just processed late; reconciliation on Nov 13 confirmed per-workspace event counts match Kafka offsets for 08:00–13:00 UTC — nothing lost, only delayed [1][3].

**What we're changing:**
- Revert `max_batch_bytes` default to 1 MB, plus a memory guard: the batcher refuses any batch larger than 25% of the container memory limit and logs a warning (bulk import keeps 10 MB via explicit config on the 2 Gi pool) — PR ingest#419 [6].
- A new alert to on-call when ingest-events consumer lag exceeds 5 minutes of events (KES-431, due Nov 20) [10].
- Config changes will go to a small canary group first [2].

Full details are in Lior's postmortem [1]. One heads-up: Orbitly is claiming an SLA service credit for the incident under their custom MSA [2][7].
